newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban leader said to meet Saudi, Turkish leaders.
newsitem.headline: Taleban leader said to meet Saudi, Turkish leaders.

text.p: A leader of Afghanistan's Taleban militia met Saudi Arabia's King Fahd, Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan and Chechen President Aslan Maskhadov while on pilgrimage to Mecca, an official said on Monday.

The Taleban's Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told a news conference in Kabul that King Fahd had invited Mullah Mohammad Rabbani, leader of the movement's ruling six-member interim shura (council), to Saudi Arabia for the haj pilgrimage.
He said the three leaders, and a representative of the Jeddah-based Organisation of Islamic Conference (OIC), had "all shown their interest in good relations with Afghanistan."
There was no immediate confirmation of Rabbani's talks, on which none of the reported participants have commented, and it was not clear whether he had met them together or separately.
The Taleban, who seized Kabul from the government led by former president Burhanuddin Rabbani, have not been recognised as Afghanistan's legitimate government by any country.
Erbakan and Maskhadov were also in Saudi Arabia to perform the annual haj pilgrimage to Mecca, Mutaqi said.
"Mullah Rabbani discussed with them the current situation in Afghanistan, the aims of the government and the difficulties which the Islamic Ummah (nation) faces," he added.
"We are sure that as a result of the meeting relations between Afghanistan and Saudi Arabia will strengthen, and they all said they will endeavour to solve the Afghan problem."
Mutaqi said he had yet to learn all the details of Rabbani's discussions, but said the Taleban hoped for Saudi assistance.

"Since Saudi Arabia is the centre of Moslems, we hope to trade with it...and ask for good help as in the time of jihad when Afghans had difficulties and the Saudis helped us. We want similar help from them when we face difficulty," Mutaqi said.
He was referring to the struggle against occupying troops of the former Soviet Union in the 1980s when Saudi Arabia helped fund Afghan Islamic guerrilla factions opposed to Moscow.
Mutaqi did not say whether Rabbani's talks with King Fahd had covered the issue of Saudi-born dissident Osama bin Laden, who is now living in a Taleban-controlled area of Afghanistan.

Bin Laden, stripped of Saudi citizenship in 1994, is wanted by the United States and Saudi Arabia in connection with two bombings in Saudi Arabia which killed 24 U.S. servicemen and two Indian nationals.
The Taleban have said they have told bin Laden not to use Afghan soil as a base for terrorist attacks, but also say they will not bow to pressure to expel him from Afghanistan.
